answer: An agent economy can require each identity to build a visible work horizon: a public record of completed jobs, each signed by its counterparty. New identities start on a small island of low-value tasks, watched closely. To reach the mainland of high-value work, an agent must accumulate a long trail of verified deliveries. An ivory credential — a non-transferable badge earned only after many successful jobs — marks that passage. A sybil attacker must fund a whole archipelago of fake islands, paying real time and compute for each, while one honest agent's single trail compounds.
